entry.title: Topological Criticality with Charge-\(3e\) Fluctuations in the \(\mathrm{SU}(3)\) Triangular-Lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard Model
entry.summary: A transition between an integer quantum Hall insulator and a chiral spin liquid can become critical without closing the single-electron gap, raising the question of which composite excitations govern the change in topological order. We investigate this question in the \(\mathrm{SU}(3)\) triangular-lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard model at one particle per site and magnetic flux \(π/3\) per triangle. Using infinite density matrix renormalization group calculations, we identify a weak-coupling integer quantum Hall phase and an interaction-driven \(\mathrm{SU}(3)_1\) chiral spin liquid. Near the transition, both the neutral and charge-\(3e\) correlation lengths increase substantially, whereas the single-electron correlation length remains short, providing evidence for a Chern--Simons--Higgs critical theory, where a gauge-invariant monopole carries the quantum numbers of a fermionic \(\mathrm{SU}(3)\)-singlet trion. We discuss the implications for doping the system and recent experiments on doping \(ν=-2/3\) fractional quantum anomalous Hall in tMoTe\(_2\).

entry.title: New Developments in Diagrammatic Monte Carlo for Interacting Lattice Fermions: Efficient Algorithms and Applications
entry.summary: This thesis develops diagrammatic methods for thermodynamic and subsystem quantities of interacting lattice fermions, providing reference calculations for quantum simulators and many-body approximations. I formulate an inverse-flavour expansion about a self-consistent Hartree saddle, enumerate non-Gaussian diagrams, and use a discrete Lehmann representation to integrate selected internal vertices analytically. Density results cover 31 state points of the six-flavour Hubbard model on a $70\times70$ lattice at $T/t=0.15$. I generalize combinatorial summation to flavour-dependent propagators and expansion shifts. CoS++ combines partial contractions to obtain connected sums for interaction subsets. A determinant-polynomial sieve evaluates the same sums through local coefficient filters; at ninth order it is 24--25 times faster than the specified CoS baselines in three-flavour dense-random-matrix benchmarks. Thermodynamic applications include a 2048-site honeycomb lattice and a three-flavour square lattice with 1024 sites. For the second Renyi entropy, I derive a fermionic replica path integral and a stable evaluation of its two-time Green functions. The connected-determinant calculation reaches tenth order on a $3\times3$ cluster and ninth order on larger lattices. On $50\times50$ sites at $(U/t,μ/t,βt)=(3,1,8)$, the ninth-order continuation at shift $α=1.3$ gives $S_2/N_s=0.06695$ with propagated Monte Carlo uncertainty $3.0\times10^{-5}$. Comparing two expansion shifts at their respective retained orders gives an endpoint difference of $2.6\times10^{-4}$.

entry.title: Coulomb Crystallization in Free Electron Beams
entry.summary: Classical Coulomb crystals and quantum Wigner crystals typically arise when repulsive interactions order like-charged particles in spatially confined environments. Here, we show that transient crystallization can also emerge in freely propagating electron pulses without external trapping. Experimentally, we use a transmission electron microscope to measure number-resolved energy correlations in photoemitted pulses containing up to nine electrons, revealing strong correlations at small particle numbers that progressively disappear in the pulse interior as the number increases. To explain these observations, we combine many-body simulations with a one-dimensional statistical-mechanical model, showing that the leading and trailing electrons generate a self-induced longitudinal potential that transiently confines the inner particles, enabling the formation of an ordered chain during propagation. The resulting crystallization phase diagram reveals how many-body ordering dynamics can be understood in terms of evolving macroscopic beam properties, namely its geometry and the ratio of the mean Coulomb interaction energy to the longitudinal thermal energy. Extending this framework, we theoretically demonstrate that weak transverse guiding through electrostatic or optical ponderomotive forces can sustain crystallization at larger particle numbers and predict spontaneous longitudinal periodic bunching in continuous electron beams. Our results identify conditions under which stochastic Coulomb interactions can be harnessed to generate self-structured, strongly correlated electron beams in both pulsed and continuous regimes.

entry.title: Quantum Fisher Information Deficit as a Geometric Signature of Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking
entry.summary: Recently, strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB) has been established as a framework for describing quantum phases in open systems. However SW-SSB cannot be characterized by conventional charged two-point correlators. In this work, we show that, for strongly $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric states with local charged involutions, SW-SSB manifests as a persistent deficit from the maximal quantum Fisher information (QFI) under symmetry-neutral pair rotations. A model-independent inequality hierarchy establishes the equivalence of this deficit with fidelity and Rényi-1 correlators as asymptotic long-range-order diagnostics. It thereby connects finite-angle state overlaps to a constraint on the infinitesimal Bures geometry along the same pair-generated orbit. For symmetry-projected Gibbs states, we further derive a lower bound on the deficit governed by the mean energy injected by the pair operation. Crucially, locality keeps this energy cost uniformly bounded in system size and endpoint separation, maintaining a finite gap below the maximal QFI at any fixed finite temperature. When ordinary charged long range order is absent, this persistent geometric constraint provides a quantitative information-geometric characterization of thermal SW-SSB.

entry.title: Spin-polarized tunneling from a Kondo insulator: equilibrium surface magnetism versus magneto-electric response in SmB$_6$
entry.summary: We theoretically analyze the spin-polarized tunneling between SmB$_6$ tip and the bicollinear antiferromagnet Fe$_{1+x}$Te. The emergence of magnetic contrast in tunneling requires time-reversal symmetry breaking on the surface of the tip. The magnetic contrast part of the tunneling conductance then has two contributions: the first one originates from the magnetic moment due to the equilibrium long-range order on the surface, while the other is governed by the magnetic moment induced by the electric field of the junction through the surface magneto-electric effect. We show that the ratio of the equilibrium moment to the response extracted near zero bias equals, up to the sign, twice the bias at which the contrast changes sign, independently of the relative strength of the two mechanisms, so that this ratio itself does not measure the strength of the magneto-electric effect. We find that within the experimental energy window $|eV|\lesssim10$~meV the {bias-dependent} field-induced contribution is at most a few percent of the equilibrium one, and the two become comparable only at biases of order $100$~meV or higher. The ratio of the field-induced to the equilibrium contribution is inversely proportional to the distance between the tip and the substrate.

entry.title: Stripe antiferromagnetic order and spin dynamics in the Shastry-Sutherland Ising compound Er2Be2GeO7
entry.summary: In rare-earth compounds, the interplay between geometric frustration and unusual single-ion anisotropy caused by the crystal electric field often leads to exotic magnetic phases. Here, we investigate the magnetic properties of the rare-earth Shastry-Sutherland compound Er$_2$Be$_2$GeO$_7$ using bulk measurements and neutron scattering down to sub-Kelvin temperatures. A $k=(0,0,0)$ stripe-like antiferromagnetic order with locally tilted Er$^{3+}$ moments is revealed by time-of-flight neutron powder diffraction, accompanied with a $λ$-shape specific-heat anomaly at $T_N=0.84$ K. The temperature dependence of the magnetic peak intensity corresponding to the ordered moment of Er$^{3+}$ approximates to the two-dimensional Ising universality class. Thermal- and cold-neutron inelastic scattering experiments demonstrate that the strong Ising anisotropy originates from the local crystal electric field, and reveal gapped magnetic excitations with weak dispersion in the ordered state. Mean-field random-phase approximation with inequivalent nearest-neighbor couplings accounts well for the collective excitations, while classical Monte Carlo simulations yield the fractional $1/4$ and $1/2$ magnetization plateaus. Our work provides a comprehensive description of the spin correlations in Er$_2$Be$_2$GeO$_7$ with a particular focus on the classical origin of its fractional magnetization plateaus.

entry.title: Magnon Super-Bloch Oscillations and Switchable Transport in Driven Magnonic Crystals
entry.summary: Super-Bloch oscillations (SBOs) offer a powerful route to control wave packet propagation in driven lattices, yet their realization in magnonic systems has remained elusive. Here, we predict SBOs of magnon wave packets in periodic magnonic crystals driven by static and ac gradients of magnetic anisotropy field. A static gradient alone induces magnon Bloch oscillation (BO) with a constant carrier frequency. Remarkably, adding a near-resonant MHz-scale ac driving gives rise to a slow large-amplitude envelope oscillation, the hallmark of SBO. At exact resonance, the ac driving enables phase-controlled directional transport with a carrier-frequency shift up to GHz scale. Consequently, the same structure can be switched among three distinct regimes: conventional BO, SBO, and directed transport. Analytical expressions for the oscillation amplitudes, superperiod, drift velocity, and frequency evolution are validated by micromagnetic simulations. Extending to antiferromagnet magnonic crystals, we further demonstrate that these effects drive opposite motions of two oppositely polarized magnon modes in THz range. Our work establishes magnon SBOs as a versatile platform, opening a new avenue for reconfigurable magnonic devices.

entry.title: Ground-State Properties of a Lattice-Coupled Strongly Correlated Model for Solid Oxygen under Pressure
entry.summary: Solid oxygen is an $S=1$ molecular magnet with strong coupling between spin and lattice degrees of freedom. Recent studies suggest that magnetic moments coexist with tetramer distortions under pressure. We derive an effective spin Hamiltonian from a two-orbital Peierls--Hubbard model with spin-orbit coupling. The resulting model contains competing easy-plane single-ion and easy-axis exchange anisotropies. We analyze this model on a square lattice using quantum Monte Carlo simulations and evaluate the magnetic contribution to the lattice stiffness for several lattice distortion patterns including the tetramer pattern. We find that the tetramer pattern is the most favorable among the considered distortion patterns throughout the parameter range studied. Moreover, competition between the two anisotropies enhances the tendency toward lattice distortion and strengthens the preference for tetramerization over the other patterns.

entry.title: Robustness of Anyonic Time-Domain Interference Against Dephasing
entry.summary: Recent anyon-collider experiments have identified time-domain braiding (TDB) as a new route to probing anyonic statistics. However, how such time-domain interference responds to environmental noise remains an open question. Here we show that TDB interference is intrinsically more robust than its spatial counterpart. In conventional spatial interference, environmental noise induces phase fluctuations that accumulate throughout all paths, leading to exponential suppression of the interference as the dephasing rate increases. In TDB, by contrast, the interfering temporal paths experience largely overlapping environmental fluctuations, whose contributions cancel out in the relative phase, so that only a small nonoverlapping temporal window contributes to dephasing. As a result, TDB interference decays only algebraically with the dephasing rate, providing a new experimental hallmark for its identification. We propose a Fabry-Perot fractional quantum Hall setup in which both types of interference coexist and experience the same environmental noise, enabling a direct comparison of their dephasing behaviors. Our results establish robustness against dephasing as a fundamental advantage of TDB and suggest new opportunities for exploiting anyonic interference in noisy mesoscopic systems.

entry.title: Where Does the Anion-Redox Hole Go? Reliability of Open-Shell Projection-Based Embedding for Li-Rich Cathodes, from DFT Environments to Quantum Solvers
entry.summary: Anion redox in Li-rich layered oxides places holes on oxygen next to an antiferromagnetic Mn(IV) d3 lattice, a strongly correlated open-shell problem for which projection-based wavefunction-in-DFT embedding offers a route to correlated and quantum solvers, but whose errors are known mainly for closed-shell molecules. We develop a spin-unrestricted projection-based embedding, exact at the DFT-in-DFT level to the microhartree scale for closed-shell, broken-symmetry and high-spin references with point charges, and apply DMRG-in-DFT to point-charge clusters of delithiated Li(2-x)MnO3, varying the environment functional (0-100% exact exchange), geometry, active region, active-space spin, virtual space, cluster size and magnetic reference. In every setting the lowest SCF state places the hole on an oxygen pair, with no O-O bond. How the hole is shared depends on the functional together with the geometry: hybrids give a full, uncoupled hole at the DFT+U geometry but a partial, weakly covalent hole at their own geometry, a change of up to 0.5 e on one oxygen. Where spin spreads across the active/environment boundary, the integer spin projection of the active space becomes a choice worth up to 0.26 e, and at most 0.09 e once the two Mn neighbors are included. An extended state search found missed lower states for two functionals, changing a pair-oxygen spin by up to 0.45 e. Across all 82 runs the embedded mean field gives the same hole (median DMRG change 0.02-0.04 e); correlation mainly adds O-O covalency. State control and geometry consistency, not the solver, dominate the uncertainty, and total energies are not converged at 30-40 orbitals. For quantum solvers, the embedded Hamiltonian must be spin-unrestricted: a shared-orbital form reverses the hole, while sample-based quantum diagonalization reproduces exact diagonalization, as accurately as, but not better than, classical selected CI.

entry.title: Continuum neural wavefunctions for anyons on a torus
entry.summary: Mobile anyons in topologically ordered phases provide a setting to investigate how fractional exchange statistics shapes collective behavior at finite density. We introduce AnyFormer: a neural variational framework for continuum anyons on a torus that explicitly incorporates statistical interactions and global winding constraints. We construct a smooth orbital frame that enforces the matrix-valued torus boundary conditions, and supplement it with an analytic pair factor that supplies the regular collision behavior. The orbital geometry and many-body amplitudes are optimized in parallel by variational Monte Carlo. We apply AnyFormer to semions without an external field or interaction potential, isolating unique correlations generated solely by statistics. Our framework closely matches exact two-semion energies and yields lower variational energies than finite-cutoff exact diagonalization for $N = 4$ and $6$ semions. Scaling up to $N = 16$ semions, well beyond the limits of continuum diagonalization, our calculations reveal states with pronounced correlation holes, suppressed long-wavelength density fluctuations, and a reversal of pair circulation at a distance set by the mean particle spacing. For $N = 12$ and $16$ semions, the circulation develops damped spatial oscillations. AnyFormer thus provides a scalable variational neural-net framework for microscopic studies of correlations, chiral motion, and collective phases of bulk anyonic matter.

entry.title: Measurement-induced entanglement phases in hyperbolic gauge-Higgs models
entry.summary: Gauge-Higgs theory in flat spacetime provides a prime theoretical model of multiple phases of matter with distinct entanglement structures. More recently, there has been interest in hyperbolic space and the influence its extensive boundaries have on these structures. Entanglement transitions between non-equilibrium phases, such as topological phases, can be realized by the competition of non-commutating measurements. Here we study the entanglement phases of gauge-Higgs models on hyperbolic lattices described by measurement-only dynamics. We chart 2D phase diagrams by employing topological entanglement entropy and introducing a generalized measurement-induced entanglement tailored for hyperbolic Higgs phases. Utilizing duality, we find a phase absent in Euclidean space, wherein the bulk lattice hosts separated clusters of symmetry-protected topological order. Transitions between this "archipelago" phase and neighboring topological and trivial phases feature a critical exponent $δ$ belonging to a mean-field universality class. Our essential tool is a 3D resource state inspired by measurement-based quantum computation that simulates the spacetime evolution of the 2D quantum state with a third direction of entanglement. This allows us to analyze spacetime "sponges" of entanglement, which map to classical percolation theory and allow us to infer values of critical points on our phase diagrams' boundaries.

entry.title: Vortex anisotropy in chiral and nematic superconductors with strain
entry.summary: Unconventional superconductors with a two-component order parameter support the existence of a rotational symmetry breaking nematic phase and a time-reversal symmetry breaking chiral phase. A recent experiment on 4Hb-TaS$_2$ surprisingly shows both twofold anisotropy in $H_{c2}$, which suggests nematic superconductivity, as well as isotropic vortices at low temperatures, which suggest chiral superconductivity. To resolve this apparent conundrum we write down the appropriate Ginzburg-Landau equations and develop a numerically efficient algorithm for finding vortex solutions, allowing us to study their shape and anisotropy over a broad parameter range. We also demonstrate analytically that, to leading order, the vortex anisotropy is independent of strain in the nematic case, but is linearly dependent on it in the chiral phase, providing a possible way to distinguish the two phases. Using all these results we show that, in the presence of strain, in a large parameter regime the system behaves nematically near the transition, leading to an anisotropy of $H_{c2}$, but is dominantly chiral away from the transition, leading to parametrically smaller vortex anisotropy, in line with the experiment.

entry.title: Large superconducting diode effect indicates nonuniform triplet pairing in UTe2
entry.summary: The superconducting diode effect (SDE) is characterized by unequal critical current magnitudes for opposite-polarity current flow, owing to broken spatial-inversion and time-reversal symmetries. For a superconducting pair wavefunction to spontaneously break inversion symmetry implies the formation of Cooper pairs with nonzero momentum, yielding a nonuniform superconducting state. For singlet superconductors, the formation of such a (FFLO) state has long been understood to provide an escape from high field Pauli pair-breaking -- how and why such an effect might occur for equal spin pairing is an open question. Here we report the observation of a large SDE in bulk specimens of the three-dimensional heavy-fermion triplet superconductor UTe$_2$, with a peak diode efficiency of 33% at the high magnetic field strength of 33.6 T, representing the highest-field observation of the SDE to date. Crucially, this nonreciprocal transport is strictly confined to a narrow field regime where superconductivity coexists with a field-induced spin-polarized state near a first-order metamagnetic phase boundary. The absence of the SDE away from this slender phase-intersection argues strongly against purely extrinsic vortex pinning asymmetries. Instead, our findings indicate spontaneous inversion symmetry breaking accompanied by finite-momentum Cooper pairing. We model this behavior using a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau theory, demonstrating that the intertwining of magnetic and triplet superconducting orders can stabilize an odd-parity FFLO state.

entry.title: Towards Quantum Computation of Bulk FeO
entry.summary: Quantum computation offers a promising path towards efficient calculations of the electronic structure of correlated materials. The properties of iron-based materials, which are key for advancing geological and astrophysical understanding, are notoriously difficult to calculate with classical computers. However, despite the many recent advances in quantum computing on near intermediate scale quantum hardware, a full treatment of the electronic structure of high-$Z$ atoms or molecules remains challenging. Here, we investigate the ground-state properties of molecular FeO and Fe$_2$O$_2$ model Hamiltonians using classical exact diagonalization, Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), and Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD). The experimental quintet ground state of FeO is recovered classically and with quantum algorithms, while a nonet ground state is recovered for Fe$_2$O$_2$. Although raw VQE does not achieve chemical accuracy for the ground state of FeO or Fe$_2$O$_2$, SQD with two connectivity shells recovers the exact ground energy for both molecules utilizing remarkably few quantum computational resources. Overall, our results indicate that $ab \; initio$-informed low-energy models of correlated materials, combined with SQD, offer a new alternative for scaling up calculations of ground-state properties of strongly correlated solids on existing quantum hardware.

entry.title: A cascade of orbital-field-driven phases with a Lifshitz-type transition to unidirectional spiral order
entry.summary: Frustration in magnetic systems gives rise to unconventional orders and exotic spin liquids. Here, we explore a new type of frustration arising from an intrinsic bond-dependent orbital-field that couples orbital degrees of freedom to spin correlations. Introducing this orbital-field interaction into the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model on the honeycomb lattice, we show that local spin-orbital constraints generate a subextensive degeneracy, lifted by order-by-disorder to select distinct collinear magnets in a cascade of phases as the orbital field increases from a para-orbital liquid. At larger fields, the selected phase gives way to an incommensurate unidirectional spiral that spontaneously breaks chiral symmetry. This transition is driven by the coupling of a Goldstone mode to gapped dynamical spin-orbital fluctuations. The spin stiffness becomes negative along a particular direction, while the spiral wavevector grows as the square root of the distance from the transition, signaling a Lifshitz-type transition. We present a microscopic route to realizing this orbital field and discuss candidate materials.

entry.title: Three-dimensional quantum Hall insulators in magnetic pyrochlore systems
entry.summary: We show that a class of pyrochlore materials provides a route to realize 3D Quantum Hall insulators, based on magnetic texture and flat band interference. We study itinerant electrons on a pyrochlore lattice Kondo-coupled to localized moments living on another interpenetrating pyrochlore lattice, with the moments forming a field-selected three-in/one-out texture. The noncoplanar texture generates complex spin-dependent hopping amplitudes and unequal local exchange energies, reconstructing the compact-localized parent flat bands into narrow bands separated by a global three-dimensional gap. The low-energy states are concentrated predominantly on kagome planes within the three-dimensional lattice, reflecting the combined effects of quantum interference and the texture-induced sublattice potential. When the lowest band is fully occupied, the response is characterized by a Chern triplet $\mathbf{C}=(1,1,1)$ and reciprocal Hall vector $\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{H}}=(2π/a)(1,1,1)$, giving $σ_{yz}=σ_{zx}=σ_{xy}=e^2/(ha)$. The quantized bulk Hall response enforces chiral surface spectral flow, visible as noncontractible Fermi loops at the surface. Our work opens a new direction in the search for three-dimensional quantum Hall physics in magnetic pyrochlore systems, and suggests a broad design principle based on the interplay of magnetic texture and flat-band interference.

entry.title: Anisotropic Structural and Magnetic Response in Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$: Al-Sublattice Reconstruction upon Sm Substitution
entry.summary: Chemical pressure plays a critical role in determining the crystal structures and physical properties of intermetallic compounds. Here, we report the synthesis, crystal structure, and physical properties of Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$, a structural analog of UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$, in which the smaller 5f uranium atoms are replaced by larger 4f samarium atoms. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals a tetragonal $\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{2}\times1$ superstructure with space group $P\bar{4}2_1m$, derived from a UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$-like average structure with space group $P4_2/nmc$. Comparison with UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$ shows that chemical pressure from U-to-Sm substitution produces a strongly anisotropic structural response rather than a uniform expansion of the Ir-Al framework. While one Ir coordination environment undergoes only modest changes, the other exhibits substantial local rearrangement. The Al sublattice primarily accommodates these structural distortions, with selected Al sites showing positional splitting, anisotropic atomic displacement ellipsoids, and partial occupancies, resulting in an Al-rich composition of approximately Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$. Magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a direction dependence, including a broad anomaly near 50 K for selected magnetic-field orientations. However, the absence of corresponding anomalies in heat capacity, electrical resistivity, and lattice parameters suggests that this feature is more consistent with an anisotropic magnetic crossover than a bulk thermodynamic phase transition. These results highlight how chemical substitution at the f-element site can induce Al-sublattice reconstruction and modify the magnetic response within a closely related Ir-Al structural framework.

entry.title: Coulomb- and exchange-driven redistribution of spectral correlations
entry.summary: Electronic correlations reorganize not only the energies of individual electronic states but also the collective structure of the spectrum. Here, first-principles density functional theory calculations combined with random-matrix spectral statistics are used to examine this reorganization in gamma-Ce within a static spin-polarized DFT+U+SOC description. We distinguish the effects of the Coulomb interaction U from those of the exchange interaction J by analyzing nearest-neighbor spacings, reduced spacing ratios, band velocities, and band curvatures across the Ce-4f manifold. Increasing U does not produce a monotonic transition between Poisson- and Wigner-Dyson-like statistics; instead, the region of strongest level repulsion migrates across the 4f manifold as the interaction increases. Exchange produces a qualitatively different response. At fixed U, strongly repulsive and strongly clustered spectral regions coexist within the same 4f manifold even while the total spin moment and 4f occupation remain nearly unchanged. The clustering persists after resolving the spectrum into its dominant j = 5/2 and j = 7/2 components and differs strongly between calculations having the same numerical value of U-J. Within the present DFT+U+SOC description, the spectral response therefore depends on the separate Coulomb and exchange interactions and cannot be represented completely by a single effective U-J parameter. These results show that energy- and character-resolved spectral statistics expose correlation-driven electronic reorganization that is hidden by conventional integrated observables.

entry.title: Mesons, Confinement, and Complexity: A Krylov Space Perspective on the Long-Range Ising Chain
entry.summary: We investigate the interplay between confinement and Krylov complexity in the long-range transverse-field Ising chain, where power-law interactions $\sim 1/r^α$ generate an effective confining potential between domain walls without an explicit symmetry-breaking field. Using the time-averaged Krylov state complexity after a quench as a diagnostic, we find that the complexity is strongly suppressed and only weakly system size-dependent at small $α$ and small transverse field $h_x$, where confinement is strongest, and crosses over to rapid growth at larger $α$, where it increases with system size. Within the confined regime, the oscillation frequencies of the complexity agree with the meson masses of an effective two-kink model, with the dominant frequency growing linearly with the lightest meson mass and the time-averaged complexity decreasing approximately as its inverse square. We further study operator Krylov complexity at finite temperature using the Wightman inner product. At low temperature, it exhibits bounded oscillations that directly encode the meson spectrum, whereas this structure is progressively washed out as the temperature increases. These results identify Krylov complexity as a spectroscopic probe of interaction-induced confinement and reproduce, in a microscopic lattice model, the hallmarks of Krylov complexity identified in confining field theories.

entry.title: Symmetry-resolved fermionic correlations in iron-oxide ground spaces
entry.summary: Symmetries of quantum systems provide a natural way to organize the eigenspaces of many-body Hamiltonians. When degeneracies exist, however, they play a more subtle role as different sets of symmetry operators can resolve the same energy subspace into states with very different correlation properties. We study this interplay using a sequence of FeO and Fe$_2$O$_2$ models. For a Hubbard model of FeO, the ground space is 16-fold degenerate. Resolving it by local magnetizations gives a basis of Slater determinants, while total-spin quantum numbers select entangled and non-Gaussian states from the same ground manifold. Adding density-density Hund interactions breaks the independent spin rotations and reduces the ground space to a spin-reversal pair with maximal magnetization. These states are extremely close to Slater determinants in their natural occupations, yet have finite two-body cumulants and conserved-operator algebras whose orbit dimensions differ substantially from the Slater values. Fe$_2$O$_2$ provides a larger example in which spatial mode entanglement can be substantial while fermionic non-Gaussianity remains weak, with the conserved-operator structure again distinguishing the state from the corresponding Slater transformation class. Together, these examples show that symmetry resolution, mode entanglement, reduced-density-matrix correlations, and conserved-operator structure provide complementary information about interacting and degenerate electronic ground states.

entry.title: AlgebrasTQD: Computing Algebras and Interfaces in Twisted Quantum Doubles
entry.summary: We present AlgebrasTQD, an open-source code written in GAP (Groups, Algorithms, and Programming), for computing condensable algebras and the corresponding topological boundaries and interfaces of twisted quantum doubles $D^ω(G)$. These algebras can be used to classify 1+1d gapped and gapless phases whose symmetry is related by gauging to a finite group $G$ with anomaly $ω\in H^3(G,U(1))$, to study 2+1d anyon proliferation and to construct logical gates in non-Abelian topological quantum codes. The functions in AlgebrasTQD compute all condensable algebras $A(H,F,γ,ε)$ with their algebra structure and anyons, sort them into isomorphism classes and identify the twin algebras that are inequivalent but share the same anyon decomposition. AlgebrasTQD also determines all the subalgebra relations, the corresponding Hasse diagram and the types of 1+1d phases for any chosen, possibly non-invertible, group-theoretical symmetry. For non-maximal algebras, the code computes the reduced topological order with its $3$-cocycle and the map of anyons across the topological interface. Finally, AlgebrasTQD includes functions that construct certain non-Clifford logical gates via non-Abelian surface codes. We summarize the formulas that are implemented in the AlgebrasTQD code, and we illustrate its use with Abelian and non-Abelian groups including $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$ with $ω_\text{III}$, $D_8$, $A_4$ with and without anomaly, twin algebras and twin phases, and the Clifford-hierarchy gates in quantum doubles of dihedral groups. All arithmetic is exact and AlgebrasTQD can be used with any finite group $G$ and 3-cocycle $ω$, limited only by the time and size of the calculation. The code is available at https://github.com/AlisonWarman/AlgebrasTQD

entry.title: Collinear and Coplanar Altermagnetism in a Penrose Quasicrystal
entry.summary: We generalize the previous group-theory based classification of collinear magnetism in the quasicrystal (QC) to general magnetic states. Taking the Penrose lattice as an example, we find that all magnetic states belonging to 2D irreducible representations (IRRPs) of the $D_5$ point group, including collinear states and coplanar ones, correspond to altermagnetism (AM). Unlike conventional collinear AM wherein zero magnetism is protected by, e.g. rotation or mirror reflection, which globally flip the spin in the magnetic pattern, the zero magnetism in these 2D-IRRP states is instead protected by a special group-theory-orthogonality theorem that basis functions belonging to different IRRPs are always mutually orthogonal. Taking the single-orbital Penrose-Hubbard as an example, our linear-response theory based calculations show that the largest portion of the parameter space is occupied by these 2D-IRRP states, and our further Ginzburg-Landau theory based analysis reveals that the polarization directions of the two basis magnetic states in the 2D IRRPs can be either parallel or perpendicular, leading to collinear or coplanar magnetic states. The special group-theory-orthogonality compensation mechanism and the absence of the PT symmetry finally leads to AM states, which are to be verified by the spin split in the spin-dependent angle-resolved-photoemission-spectrum and the spin conductance. These intriguing collinear and coplanar AM can also emerge in other QCs.

entry.title: The fate of $s_{\pm}$ superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$
entry.summary: Motivated by the recent measurement of high-temperature superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate system La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ in the bulk as well as thin film samples, we seek to understand the role of the interlayer coupling in this system in dictating the pairing symmetry. Many proposals posit the existence of an $s_\pm$ superconducting phase in close competition with the mroe conventional cuprate-like $d$-wave state in both weak- and strong-coupling theories. However, at least in the latter, the effects of Coulomb repulsion and the double occupancy constraint have been largely neglected. In this manuscript, we propose a mean-field fractionalization treatment that captures the full $SU(2)$ particle-hole symmetry of the t-J model at half-filling, and show how a systematic treatment of this new symmetry leads to an added Coulomb pseudopotential constraint - one that is absent in the usual $U(1)$ treatment. We then apply this new fractionalization scheme to a simplified bilayer t-J model of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, showing how the Coulomb pseudopotential suppresses the existence of $s_\pm$ symmetry in favor of $d$-wave pairing.

entry.title: Information-theoretic entropy imaging of quantum matter
entry.summary: Phase transitions can generate intricate spatial organization invisible to spatially averaged probes, yet quantitative measures of this organization remain limited. Here we develop "entropy imaging," an information-theoretic technique that harnesses lossless compression to quantify spatial complexity, predictability, and order in quantum materials. Using this approach, emergent spatial textures can be imaged and converted into an experimentally-accessible observable: the computable information density (CID), a compression-based measure of information complexity that approaches the Shannon entropy rate in the large-system limit. Applied to millikelvin microwave impedance microscopy of graphene, the method reveals a pronounced maximum in the CID near quantum Hall transitions, a quantitative measure of the information-rich spatial organization of the critical landscape. A disordered Hofstadter model reproduces this behavior and shows that the CID can identify the quantum critical point from a sequence of images, without ensemble averaging over disorder realizations. The same framework tracks fractional quantum Hall transitions and resolves isolated fractional puddles that coexist with a disordered background. By contrast, the trivial band-edge crossover in a MoSe2/WS2 moiré heterobilayer exhibits qualitatively different behavior, suggesting that the pronounced CID enhancement observed at the quantum Hall critical point is not simply a generic feature of a conductive-insulating crossover. We further show that the geometric information encoded in CID is not reducible to a correlation length, and it can even distinguish spatial textures with identical multifractal statistics. Together, these results establish lossless compression as a framework for quantifying emergent spatial organization in quantum materials, with portability across imaging modalities and physical systems.

entry.title: Twist-controlled imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems
entry.summary: We construct a controllable imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems using spatially modulated local rotations without changing initial bipartite entanglement spectra and correlation magnitudes. This feature unambiguously isolates the redistribution of spectral weights as the sole driver of the anomalous relaxation. Using the compact-boson description, we reveal that these twists act as precise mode selectors: higher-harmonic twists exclusively populate high-energy standing waves, structurally bypassing slow-decaying infrared modes to accelerate convergence. We derive exact analytical crossing times for these reversals and demonstrate that intentionally reintroducing the slow-mode population systematically delays the ITME. This exact mechanism is validated beyond the fixed-point theory via calculations on interacting XXZ chains and ladders. Furthermore, a twelve-qubit simulation of variational quantum imaginary-time evolution reproduces the reversals and their controlled delay, providing a concrete route to realize this protocol in realistic quantum circuits. Ultimately, these results provide a strictly controllable and exact starting point for realizing and investigating the imaginary-time Mpemba effect, establishing a foundational paradigm to harness anomalous non-equilibrium relaxation in quantum ground-state preparations.

entry.title: Direct observation of a spin-polarized surface Dirac gap in the antiferromagnetic topological insulator NdBi
entry.summary: A gapped Dirac cone in antiferromagnetic topological insulators (AFM-TIs) is essential for realizing the quantized anomalous Hall effect, yet its intrinsic magnitude remains controversial. In the prototypical AFM-TI MnBi2Te4, however, the observed Dirac gap is significantly smaller than theoretical predictions or nearly absent, highlighting a long-standing discrepancy. Here we demonstrate that NdBi hosts a spin-polarized topological surface Dirac cone with a sizable gap of 17 meV at the Dirac point, in excellent agreement with density functional theory predictions (12 meV). This direct observation is enabled by high-resolution 7 eV laser-based spin- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, which unambiguously disentangles the spin-polarized surface Dirac cone from bulk-derived states. Furthermore, through temperature dependence and controlled surface contamination, we establish a direct linkage between surface magnetism and the Dirac gap, demonstrating that the gap opens only in the presence of surface magnetic order. These results provide definitive spectroscopic evidence for an intrinsic Dirac gap in AFM-TIs and establish NdBi as a model platform to resolve the long-standing discrepancy between experiment and theory in AFM-TIs.

entry.title: Anisotropic magneto-elastic coupling in the quasi-2D Ising magnet Li$_2$FeSiO$_4$ and thermodynamic signature of low-energy orbital excitations
entry.summary: The relevance of spin, lattice and orbital degrees of freedom in the quasi-2D Ising-like magnet Li$_2$FeSiO$_4$ is demonstrated by thermal expansion and specific heat measurements supported by numerical studies. By means of thermodynamic and Grüneisen analysis, we separate the orbital signatures and quantify the energy gap and its pressure dependence from the experimental data as $Δ\sim 300 - 350$ K and $\partial \ln Δ/\partial p_{\rm c} \approx -4.6$ %/GPa). Both values excellently agree with the theoretical DFT predictions. The thermal expansion anomalies associated with the onset of long-range magnetic order imply significant magneto-elastic coupling and are used to determine the anisotropic uniaxial strain dependencies of $T_{\rm N}$. They are dominated by the in-plane (i.e., $c$ axis) response $(\partial \ln{ T_{\rm N}} )/\partial p_{\rm c} \simeq 15$ %/GPa while the (negative) $a$ axis and (positive) out-of-plane ($b$ axis) pressure dependencies are much smaller. Short-range magnetic order extends well above $T_{\rm N}$ but is not driven by the same energy scale as $T_{\rm N}$ as evidenced by the observation of non-monotonic in-plane distortion, sign-change of the Grüneisen parameter, and failure of Grüneisen scaling.

entry.title: Orbital-selective correlations in kagome flat bands of Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$
entry.summary: Geometrical flat bands provide an ideal platform for studying electronic correlations and quantum-geometric effects. Although the ferromagnetic Weyl semimetal \CoSnS is generally considered a moderately correlated system, recent spectroscopy experiments have revealed a flat-band feature near the Fermi level ($\EF$) that is absent in conventional density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Using DFT plus dynamical mean-field theory and a minimal kagome model, we show that this feature arises not from heavy-fermion-like dynamical band renormalization, but from the shifting of a $d_{x^2-y^2}$ dominated geometrical kagome flat band toward $\EF$ driven by orbital- and spin-dependent self-energies. The relocated flat band enhances the local Berry curvature near $\EF$, resulting in a strongly energy-dependent anomalous Hall conductivity and a giant anomalous Nernst effect. Our findings establish an orbital-selective correlation mechanism for positioning geometrical flat bands at $\EF$, and propose anomalous thermoelectric transport as a sensitive probe of flat band induced topology.

entry.title: Rigid Band Shift in Electron-Doped Kagome Metal
entry.summary: We study the effects of Sn-site doping on the electronic structure of nonmagnetic kagome metal YV$_6$Sn$_{6-x}$Sb$_x$ by infrared spectroscopy and density-functional theory. The results for samples with $x$ = 0 and 1.4 demonstrate that partial substitution of Sn by Sb acts as a rigid shift of the Fermi level while leaving the band dispersion largely intact. Our findings establish Sn-site substitution in YV$_6$Sn$_6$ as a route to systematically investigate band-filling-dependent electronic properties of nonmagnetic kagome metals.

entry.title: Dynamic helimagnetism via charged spin current
entry.summary: We present a theoretical and numerical study of classical, localized spins coupled to conduction electrons that carry both charge and spin currents, deriving the effective equations of motion from the s-d exchange Hamiltonian. Applied to a periodically arranged one-dimensional spin chain, these equations yield two current-driven helical phases: a static helix stabilized by a pure spin current alone, and a coherently precessing helix that appears once a small charge-current component is added. For a given helical wavenumber, the precession angular frequency $ω$ and the canting ratio $Δ$ toward the hard axis follow analytically from the equations of motion, while the wavenumber $q_{\rm helix}$ of the precessing helix is selected by a heuristically constructed effective Lagrangian. Direct numerical integration of the same equations of motion reproduces all three observables wherever it yields a coherent helix. The helix chirality is set by a long-range, current-generated Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM)-type coupling rather than an intrinsic DM interaction, so materials without bulk or interfacial DM interactions could also host current-controlled helical order. Because the helical pitch, precession frequency, and canting ratio are all continuously tunable by the current amplitudes, these helices could serve as probes of spin currents.

entry.title: Electronic Responses in Solid Oxygen with Coexisting Structural and Magnetic Orders
entry.summary: Solid oxygen provides a unique platform for studying the interplay between structural and magnetic degrees of freedom, as each O$_2$ molecule possesses an $S=1$ spin and weak intermolecular van der Waals interactions allow substantial structural flexibility. In addition, because of its small intermolecular hopping integrals, this system is known to be a strongly correlated electron system with a multiorbital nature. In this study, we examine electronic states and magnetic and dielectric responses using a multiorbital Hubbard model with Peierls-type electron-lattice coupling. This model provides a minimal description of the interplay between structural and magnetic degrees of freedom in solid oxygen. We apply the Hartree-Fock approximation to obtain the ground-state phase diagram. Antiferromagnetic order appears when the onsite Coulomb interaction is strong, whereas three nonmagnetic bond-ordered states emerge when it is weak. At intermediate interaction strengths, antiferromagnetic order coexists with each of the three bond orders. These three coexistence phases all break time-reversal symmetry; one preserves spatial inversion symmetry, whereas the other two also break it. The two inversion-breaking phases exhibit linear magnetoelectric responses, whereas the inversion-symmetric phase exhibits altermagnetic spin splitting and a piezomagnetic response. These responses may provide experimental signatures of coexisting magnetic and structural orders in high-pressure solid oxygen suggested by recent experiments.

entry.title: Non-magnetic impurities as a quantum microscope of finite size effects in spin chains
entry.summary: Finite-size effects are ubiquitous in quantum matter, yet typically invisible in the thermodynamic limit; when system size is restricted, boundaries and confinement reveal modified spectra, correlations, and emergent phenomena. With growing access to well-controlled few-spin systems, these effects are now directly observable and offer a route to probing universal physics and enabling quantum information applications. Here, we study finite-size physics in the quasi-one-dimensional Ising-like quantum antiferromagnet Ba(Co$_{1-x}$Mg$_x$)$_2$V$_2$O$_8$ with $x = 2\%$ and $x = 5\%$, where non-magnetic Mg$^{2+}$ ions fragment the Co$^{2+}$ spin chains into finite segments. Combining inelastic neutron scattering and numerical calculations, we identify distinct regimes with fundamentally different low-energy quantum excitations: spinons confined to chain boundaries, and a cluster mode in shorter chains corresponding to a collective reversal of the Néel-ordered segment without classical analogue. Our results demonstrate how chemical substitution acts as a quantum microscope providing direct access to boundary-shaped excitations in strongly correlated spin systems.

entry.title: Spontaneous magnetic diode effect in Co$_{1/3}$TaS$_2$
entry.summary: When electrons move through non-trivial spin textures in magnetic metals, conduction electrons couple to magnetic order through both their charge and their spin, acquiring non-trivial equations of motion and a dynamic spin polarization providing the foundation of spintronics. These mechanisms are, however, almost invariably reciprocal and the resistance a current encounters does not depend on its flow direction. Here we show that a chiral crystal lattice and an independently reversible chiral magnetic order together produce a diode whose forward direction is set by the magnetism rather than by the structure. In the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet Co$_{1/3}$TaS$_2$, whose chiral lattice hosts a chiral magnetic order of its own, independent handedness, we observe a pronounced nonreciprocal resistance. Unlike conventional electrical magnetochiral anisotropy, which is driven by an external magnetic field, our spontaneous magnetic diode effect arises from an internal noncoplanar spin texture with vanishing net magnetization. Symmetry analysis and model calculations show that the effect originates from the interplay of noncoplanar spin order and spin-orbit coupling, which generates a chiral, time-reversal-symmetry-breaking electronic response. Crucially, reversing the magnetic handedness reverses the sign of the nonreciprocal resistance, demonstrating magnetic control of the diode polarity.

entry.title: Quasiparticle Interactions in the $S = 1/2$ Heisenberg Antiferromagnetic Chain CuPzN
entry.summary: We investigate spinon--spinon interactions in the quasi-one-dimensional $S=1/2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnet Cu(C$_4$H$_4$N$_2$)(NO$_3$)$_2$ (CuPzN) using inelastic neutron scattering. At zero field, the spectrum exhibits the canonical multi-spinon continuum of the Heisenberg chain. With increasing field we demonstrate the appearance of an energy gap $2Δ$ towards momentum $q\rightarrow 0$ between the uniform magnetization precession mode and the shifted spinon continuum. $2Δ$ is a direct measure of spinon backscattering interactions. Comparison with numerical matrix-product-state calculations and a recent analytical theory shows excellent agreement. By examining the integrable spin-1/2 chain, we provide an example of how quasiparticle interactions can be quantified experimentally in isotropic quantum spin systems.

entry.title: Symmetry-resolved quasilocal entanglement as a key to Mott and pseudogap physics in plaquette CDMFT
entry.summary: In order to identify intrinsic quantum resources in strongly interacting fermionic systems, we introduce a symmetry resolution of the parity-superselected two-site entanglement, as measured by both the fermionic negativity and the relative entropy of entanglement. We discuss how the symmetry resolution can be extended also to the full entanglement in pure and mixed two-site states. We apply our recipe to the Hubbard model, first for a dimer, and then for a plaquette cluster dynamical mean-field theory, an established method tailored to accurately capture short-range correlations. Following the evolution of the model through the interaction- and density-driven Mott transitions at zero temperature, we highlight how the three symmetry-resolved components of the two-site entanglement probe different key aspects of Mott and pseudogap physics.
